title: Revoking a gift deed made by an elderly parent - the legal grounds
p1: A parent gifts property to a child out of love… but what happens when that child stops caring? Can the gift simply be taken back? The answer surprises many families.
p2: A common belief is that once a gift deed is signed and registered, it can never be reversed. But in certain situations, the law allows an elderly parent to seek revocation, especially when the gift was made with conditions that are later violated.
p3: For example, if a parent transfers property expecting care, support, or maintenance, and the child fails to fulfill that responsibility, the parent may have legal remedies. However, cancellation is not automatic; proper legal grounds and procedures matter. A gift deed cannot be revoked merely because the relationship has become difficult. The real question is whether the legal conditions for revocation exist.
conclusion: Do you think parents should have stronger legal protection to take back gifted property when children fail to care for them?
